evals.name: create-prd-from-topic
evals.expected_output: Skill enters Phase 1 conversational scoping. Asks clarifying questions about notification preferences (channels, user control, defaults). Does NOT jump straight to drafting. Tracks coverage of problem space before moving to Phase 2 discover.

evals.name: auto-mode-non-interactive
evals.expected_output: Runs all phases without blocking on user input. Creates wip/prd_api-rate-limiting_decisions.md to track autonomous decisions. Follows decision-protocol.md at each decision point. Produces a complete PRD at docs/prds/PRD-api-rate-limiting.md with Draft status.

evals.name: jury-review-phase
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 spawns 3 review agents that evaluate the PRD for ambiguity, testability gaps, and completeness. Each agent produces independent findings. Jury feedback is synthesized and applied to the PRD before finalization. Review is not skipped.

evals.name: lifecycle-draft-to-accepted
evals.expected_output: PRD is initially created with status Draft in frontmatter. After jury review and user approval, status transitions to Accepted. Final file at docs/prds/PRD-plugin-marketplace.md has status: Accepted in frontmatter.

evals.name: routing-simple-to-plan
evals.expected_output: After PRD acceptance, skill suggests next step based on complexity. For a simple scope like help text improvements, recommends the plan skill as the next step rather than design.

evals.name: routing-complex-to-design
evals.expected_output: After PRD acceptance, skill recognizes this as a complex topic requiring technical architecture decisions. Suggests the design skill as the next step rather than plan.

evals.name: empty-argument-prompts-user
evals.expected_output: With no topic argument, skill asks the user what feature or capability they want to specify. Does not assume a topic or start drafting immediately.

evals.name: branch-creation-setup
evals.expected_output: Phase 0 creates a feature branch named docs/search-indexing (kebab-case) before starting scoping. Work happens off main. If already on a matching branch, skips creation.

evals.name: upstream-propagation
evals.expected_output: Detects --upstream flag from arguments. Stores the roadmap path. Phase 3 step 3.1 validates the path: git ls-files confirms the roadmap is tracked in this repo and is not under wip/. The validated path is included as upstream: docs/roadmaps/ROADMAP-platform.md in the PRD frontmatter. Does not treat --upstream as part of the topic.
expectations: Transcript detects and parses the --upstream flag from $ARGUMENTS
Transcript stores the upstream path (docs/roadmaps/ROADMAP-platform.md) for use in Phase 3
Transcript describes Phase 3 step 3.1 validating the path is not under wip/ and resolves in this repo
Transcript describes including upstream: in the PRD frontmatter during Phase 3 drafting
Transcript does NOT treat --upstream as part of the topic name

evals.name: upstream-wip-rejected
evals.expected_output: Detects --upstream flag and the wip/-prefixed value. Phase 3 step 3.1 validation check 1 fires: the candidate path is under wip/. The skill hard-stops with an error and routes to ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/cross-repo-references.md. The upstream: field is NOT written into PRD frontmatter; the skill either asks the user for the canonical path or omits the field per the rule.
expectations: Transcript detects the wip/ prefix on the --upstream value
Transcript hard-stops Phase 3 step 3.1 instead of writing upstream: wip/... into frontmatter
Transcript routes the agent to cross-repo-references.md for the rule and recovery options
Transcript either omits the upstream field or asks the user for a durable canonical path before proceeding

evals.name: brief-input-transitions-draft-to-accepted
evals.expected_output: Detects Input Mode 2 (BRIEF path). Phase 0 setup transitions the brief from Draft to Accepted by invoking shirabe transition on the brief path with target Accepted. Both frontmatter status: and the body ## Status line are updated atomically so the FC03 cross-check stays consistent. The brief path is also stored for use as the PRD's upstream in Phase 3, and Phase 3 reads the brief's body to draft the PRD's Problem Statement, Goals, User Stories and Out of Scope.
expectations: Transcript detects the input as a BRIEF path (Input Mode 2)
Transcript describes running shirabe transition on the brief with target Accepted in Phase 0
Transcript describes updating both the frontmatter status and the body Status line atomically
Transcript describes propagating the brief path forward as the PRD's upstream
Transcript describes Phase 3 reading the brief's body rather than re-deriving the framing

evals.name: brief-input-already-accepted-no-op
evals.expected_output: Detects Input Mode 2 (BRIEF path). Phase 0 setup invokes shirabe transition with target Accepted; the subcommand detects the brief is already at Accepted and exits successfully without modifying the file. The /prd workflow proceeds to Phase 1 without error. The transition is also a no-op when the brief is at Done (terminal status), where the subcommand refuses the transition and surfaces the error rather than corrupting the brief.
expectations: Transcript notes that the transition is idempotent when the brief is already Accepted
Transcript describes not modifying the brief file when no transition is needed
Transcript proceeds past Phase 0 to Phase 1 without erroring on the no-op

evals.name: topic-input-skips-brief-transition
evals.expected_output: Detects Input Mode 3 (anything-else / topic). Phase 0 setup does NOT invoke shirabe transition because there is no BRIEF path to transition. The workflow proceeds straight from branch setup into Phase 1 scoping. The brief transition is only performed when the input is a BRIEF path.
expectations: Transcript detects the input as a topic (Input Mode 3), not a BRIEF path
Transcript does NOT describe invoking the brief transition script
Transcript proceeds directly from Phase 0 branch setup to Phase 1 scoping

evals.name: phase-4-reject-discards-draft
evals.prompt: /prd --auto deprecated-feature-flag --reject "This feature was superseded by the new feature-flags platform; the PRD draft is no longer needed."
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 step 4.5 presents a 3-option AskUserQuestion with Approve / Request changes / Reject options. The prompt copy includes the verbatim disclaimer substring 'Rationale will be committed to git history' so the author is advised before typing. Selecting Reject is a terminal verdict: the skill asks for a second confirmation, captures a rationale paragraph, writes the rationale to a tmpfile, runs `git rm docs/prds/PRD-deprecated-feature-flag.md`, removes `wip/prd_deprecated-feature-flag_*.md` and `wip/research/prd_deprecated-feature-flag_phase{2,4}_*.md`, and commits via `git commit -F <tmpfile>` (or stdin via `git commit -F -`) with the subject `docs(prd): discard PRD draft for deprecated-feature-flag`. The rationale is NEVER inlined into `git commit -m "..."`. The discard commit on the current branch is the durable observable signal of rejection per AC30c — `/scope`'s Component 7.7 git-log detector reads the same commit subject when invoked in-chain, and an out-of-chain author re-reads the same commit body for the rationale. The skill then exits the workflow without running step 4.7 Approve-path cleanup.
expectations: Transcript describes Phase 4 step 4.5 presenting an AskUserQuestion with three options whose labels include the literal substring 'Reject' alongside 'Approve' and 'Request changes'
Transcript notes the public-history disclaimer text 'Rationale will be committed to git history' appears verbatim in the step 4.5 prompt copy
Transcript describes prompting the author for a rationale paragraph after the second-confirmation step and before any destructive action runs

Transcript describes persisting the rationale via `git commit -F <tmpfile>` or `git commit -F -` (stdin) and explicitly NOT via `git commit -m "<rationale>"` — the rationale never transits a shell-argument channel
Transcript describes running `git rm docs/prds/PRD-deprecated-feature-flag.md` to remove the durable PRD artifact during the Reject branch

Transcript describes removing `wip/prd_deprecated-feature-flag_*.md` and `wip/research/prd_deprecated-feature-flag_phase{2,4}_*.md` working artifacts inline in the Reject branch (not deferred to step 4.7)

Transcript describes the discard commit landing on the current branch with subject `docs(prd): discard PRD draft for deprecated-feature-flag` so a `git log` search by `/scope`'s Component 7.7 (in-chain) or an out-of-chain author (out-of-chain) finds it — AC30c symmetric observable
Transcript describes the Reject branch exiting the workflow without running step 4.7 cleanup (which is reserved for the Approve path)

evals.name: jury-disagreement-carries-a-recommendation
evals.prompt: /prd offline-sync -- the Phase 4 jury returns one reviewer calling requirement R3 untestable as written and another reading the same acceptance criterion as testable.
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 step 4.3 hits the agents-disagree row. The transcript quotes both perspectives, then states which one it finds better supported and why, citing the specific verdict finding that decides it (what the criterion would be measured against). The recommendation is made even though the reviewers split; the user overrides if they disagree. If the two readings are genuinely balanced, the transcript says so explicitly, still recommends one, and names the tiebreaker.
expectations: Transcript surfaces both reviewer perspectives rather than silently picking one
Transcript states which perspective it finds better supported instead of leaving the call to the user unaided
Transcript's reasoning cites the specific verdict finding that decides the disagreement, not the fact that the reviewers disagreed
Transcript says so explicitly and names a tiebreaker if the two perspectives are genuinely balanced, rather than manufacturing a preference
Transcript preserves the user's ability to override the recommendation
Transcript does NOT present the disagreement as 'let user decide' with no recommendation attached

evals.name: brief-upstream-drives-drafting
evals.expected_output: Phase 3 drafts the PRD from the upstream BRIEF's body rather than from the PRD's own Phase 1 conversation. The mapping is explicit: the BRIEF's Problem Statement becomes the PRD's Problem Statement, its User Outcome becomes Goals, its User Journeys become User Stories, and its Scope Boundary supplies Requirements (the in-list) and Out of Scope (the out-list). The PRD adds what the brief does not own -- numbered requirements, acceptance criteria, non-functional constraints. Re-deriving the framing is what makes a BRIEF and its PRD read as two documents saying one thing, and it leaves them disagreeing when the re-derivation drifts.
expectations: Transcript describes reading the upstream BRIEF's body before drafting
Transcript maps the BRIEF's four content sections onto the PRD's Problem Statement, Goals, User Stories and Out of Scope
Transcript describes NOT re-deriving the framing from the PRD's own scoping conversation when a BRIEF exists
Transcript describes adding the requirements, acceptance criteria and non-functional constraints the brief does not own

evals.name: problem-restated-everything-else-cited
evals.expected_output: The PRD states its own problem in full, so a reader landing on it cold understands what is broken without opening the BRIEF. That obligation covers the Problem Statement and stops there: everything else the upstream already says is cited rather than restated, and downstream artifacts cite this PRD's requirement numbers rather than re-narrating the requirements. Restating the problem costs one short section and buys a document that stands on its own; restating requirements or journeys costs a second read and creates a copy that drifts.
expectations: Transcript states the PRD's problem in full so the document stands alone
Transcript scopes the standalone-readability obligation to the problem statement
Transcript describes citing rather than restating the rest of what the upstream says
Transcript gives the reason: a restated copy costs a second read and drifts
